The `getAbsolutePath` method, as per the Javadoc, can throw a `SecurityException` if a required system property value cannot be accessed. In the given code, there is no check or validation to avoid the `SecurityException`. The `SecurityException` is a checked exception, and it is not caught or handled in the code. Therefore, if the `getAbsolutePath` method throws a `SecurityException`, it will propagate up and may cause the program to terminate abnormally unless it is caught at a higher level.
